title: Export a discussion of any depth

blocks.text: The community site exports a discussion for the moderation team: every comment in the order the site shows them, and how deep the longest chain of replies goes. Last week a spam bot answered its own replies 180,000 times, and the export of that one discussion killed the export worker with a `StackOverflowError`. The first suggestion in the team channel was to start the whole service with `-Xss64m`.
`Comment` and `summary(...)` are done. Finish the two `TODO`s in `src/main/java/practice/Discussion.java`:

items: `deepest(...)`: the number of levels in the longest chain of replies, the root being level 1;
`inOrder(...)`: every comment's id in display order. A comment comes first, then the whole thread under its oldest reply, then the thread under its next reply, and so on.

blocks.text: When you're done, any discussion exports on the worker's ordinary threads, the bot's included, with no change to the service's stack size. About fifteen lines in total.
The tests run each export on a thread with a 1 MB stack.

cases.says: a short branching discussion is counted, listed with its root first, and summarised
a comment with no replies is one level and lists only itself
the depth of a chain of 250,000 replies is measured on a thread with a 1 MB stack
a chain of 250,000 replies is listed on a thread with a 1 MB stack
replies are listed oldest first, each followed by the whole thread under it

origin.section: -Xss Sets How Many Frames Fit, So Recursion as Deep as the Data Fails on Large Input

concepts: -Xss decides how many frames fit, and the depth changes with frame size and JIT compilation, so a recursion as deep as its input overflows on some input while a loop or an explicit stack on the heap doesn't; a bigger -Xss only moves the limit.
Java has no tail-call elimination: a recursive call in the last position still pushes a frame.
